topicName: OS-Level Performance Metrics (CPU, Memory, Disk I/O, Network)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"OS-Level Performance Metrics: A Performance Testing Guide"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"During performance testing, analyzing application metrics alone is insufficient. Operating System (OS) level metrics provide the ground truth regarding how hardware resources are consumed under load. This tutorial covers the four pillars of OS-level performance metrics: CPU, Memory, Disk I/O, and Network."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. CPU Metrics"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"CPU utilization measures the percentage of time the processor is busy executing non-idle tasks. However, high CPU usage is not always bad; it is important to analyze the breakdown of CPU time."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"User Time (us): Time spent executing user-level applications and processes."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"System Time (sy): Time spent executing kernel-level code, such as system calls and driver operations."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Wait Time (wa): Time the CPU spends waiting for I/O operations to complete. High 'wa' indicates a storage or network bottleneck."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Load Average: The number of processes queued for the CPU or waiting on disk I/O over 1, 5, and 15-minute intervals."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Memory Metrics"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Memory metrics help identify memory leaks, insufficient RAM, and excessive swapping which severely degrades application performance."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Free vs. Available Memory: Free memory is completely unused, while available memory includes space that can be reclaimed if processes request it."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Swap In/Out: The rate at which data is transferred between physical RAM and swap space on the disk. Frequent swapping indicates severe memory pressure."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Disk I/O Metrics"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Storage bottlenecks can stall applications even if CPU and memory are underutilized. Key metrics include throughput, IOPS, and latency."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second): The number of read and write operations executed per second."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Throughput (MB/s): The volume of data read from or written to the disk per second."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Await Time: The average time (in milliseconds) for I/O requests to be serviced, including queue time and device service time."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Network Metrics"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Network metrics ensure that the network interface card (NIC) and underlying infrastructure are not dropping packets or bottlenecking traffic."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Bandwidth Utilization: The volume of data transmitted and received relative to network capacity."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Packet Loss: The percentage of packets sent that fail to reach their destination, causing retransmissions."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Interface Errors: Errors on incoming (rx) and outgoing (tx) packets, often indicating hardware or driver issues."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Linux Commands for OS Monitoring"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can capture these metrics using standard Linux command-line utilities during a performance test run."},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"top
# Interactive process viewer for CPU and memory usage

vmstat 2
# Reports virtual memory statistics every 2 seconds

iostat -xz 2
# Extended disk statistics and utilization metrics

sar -n DEV 1 10
# Network throughput and packet analysis"}]
